theory.intro: **Power** is the rate at which an appliance uses electricity, measured in watts (W), where $1000\text{ W} = 1\text{ kW}$. **Energy** used is measured in kilowatt hours, and $\text{kWh} = \text{kW} \times \text{hours}$.
facts: Divide watts by $1000$ to get kilowatts, so a $2400$ W heater is a $2.4$ kW heater.
Multiply kilowatts by $1000$ to get back to watts, so $0.75$ kW is $750$ W.
Divide minutes by $60$ to get hours before multiplying, so $45$ minutes is $0.75$ h.
Energy in kilowatt hours is $\text{kWh} = \text{kW} \times \text{h}$, so the power must be in kW and not in watts.
Running cost is $\text{cost} = \text{kWh} \times \text{price per kWh}$, with a price in cents divided by $100$ first.
steps: Multiply the kilowatts by the hours to find the energy in kWh
Multiply the energy by the price per kWh when a cost is asked for

foundation.question_text: A fan heater is rated at $2400$ W. Express this power in kilowatts.
A blender is rated at $0.85$ kW. Express this power in watts.
A $3$ kW electric oven is used for $4$ hours. How much energy does it use, in kilowatt hours?
A $1500$ W heater is switched on for $40$ minutes. How much energy does it use, in kilowatt hours?
A $60$ W desk lamp is left on for $5$ hours. How much energy does it use, in kilowatt hours?
A $250$ W television is switched on for $90$ minutes. How much energy does it use, in kilowatt hours?
An appliance uses $18$ kWh of energy. Electricity costs $\$0.28$ per kWh. What does it cost to run?
A $2$ kW electric frypan is used for $3$ hours. Electricity costs $31$ cents per kWh. What does it cost to run?

development.question_text: A $3.6$ kW clothes dryer is run for $50$ minutes. Electricity is charged at $28$ cents per kWh. What does this cost?
A $1200$ W dishwasher runs for $1$ hour $30$ minutes, four times a week. Electricity costs $34$ cents per kWh. What is the cost of running it for one week, to the nearest cent?
development.solution_text:
$1200\text{ W} = 1.2\text{ kW}$
$\text{energy per run} = 1.2 \times 1.5$
$= 1.8\text{ kWh}$
$\text{energy per week} = 1.8 \times 4$
$= 7.2\text{ kWh}$
$\text{cost} = 7.2 \times \$0.34$
$= \$2.448$
$\approx \$2.45$

development.question_text: A $2000$ W air conditioner runs for $5$ hours a day for $30$ days. Electricity costs $\$0.29$ per kWh. What is the total cost?
development.solution_text:
$2000\text{ W} = 2\text{ kW}$
$\text{energy per day} = 2 \times 5$
$= 10\text{ kWh}$
$\text{energy for }30\text{ days} = 10 \times 30$
$= 300\text{ kWh}$
$\text{cost} = 300 \times \$0.29$
$= \$87$

development.question_text: An office runs $8$ desktop computers, each rated at $150$ W, for $9$ hours a day. How much energy do they use in one day, in kilowatt hours?
A warehouse has $24$ lights, each rated at $45$ W, switched on for $11$ hours a day. How much energy do they use in a $7$-day week, in kilowatt hours?
development.solution_text:
$\text{total power} = 24 \times 45$
$= 1080\text{ W}$
$= 1.08\text{ kW}$
$\text{energy per day} = 1.08 \times 11$
$= 11.88\text{ kWh}$
$\text{energy per week} = 11.88 \times 7$
$= 83.16\text{ kWh}$

development.question_text: Running a $1.6$ kW pool pump cost $\$27.90$ when electricity was charged at $\$0.25$ per kWh. For how many hours was the pump running?
A $900$ W games console used $21.6$ kWh of energy over one month. For how many hours was it switched on?
Heater Model A is rated at $2400$ W and Model B at $2000$ W. Each is run for $6$ hours a day for $90$ days, with electricity at $\$0.30$ per kWh. How much more does Model A cost to run?
development.solution_text:
$\text{difference in power} = 2400 - 2000$
$= 400\text{ W}$
$= 0.4\text{ kW}$
$\text{hours} = 6 \times 90$
$= 540\text{ h}$
$\text{extra energy} = 0.4 \times 540$
$= 216\text{ kWh}$
$\text{extra cost} = 216 \times \$0.30$
$= \$64.80$

mastery.question_text: Every day a $900$ W microwave oven is used for $20$ minutes at $50\%$ power. Electricity is charged at $\$0.32$ per kWh. What is the cost of running the microwave for $365$ days?
mastery.solution_text:
$900\text{ W} = 0.9\text{ kW}$
$\text{power used} = 0.9 \times 0.5$
$= 0.45\text{ kW}$
$20\text{ min} = \dfrac{20}{60}\text{ h}$
$\text{energy per day} = 0.45 \times \dfrac{20}{60}$
$= 0.15\text{ kWh}$
$\text{energy for }365\text{ days} = 0.15 \times 365$
$= 54.75\text{ kWh}$
$\text{cost} = 54.75 \times \$0.32$
$= \$17.52$

mastery.question_text: A standard refrigerator uses $620$ kWh per year. An energy-efficient model costs $\$470$ more to buy and uses $385$ kWh per year. Electricity costs $\$0.40$ per kWh. After how many years does the saving on electricity cover the extra purchase price?
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{energy saved each year} = 620 - 385$
$= 235\text{ kWh}$
$\text{saving each year} = 235 \times \$0.40$
$= \$94$
$\text{time} = \dfrac{470}{94}$
$= 5\text{ years}$

mastery.question_text: A $2500$ W vacuum cleaner uses $338$ kWh of energy over a year of $52$ weeks. On average, how many hours and minutes is it used each week?
mastery.solution_text:
$2500\text{ W} = 2.5\text{ kW}$
$\text{energy per week} = \dfrac{338}{52}$
$= 6.5\text{ kWh}$
$\text{time} = \dfrac{6.5}{2.5}$
$= 2.6\text{ h}$
$0.6\text{ h} = 0.6 \times 60$
$= 36\text{ min}$
The vacuum cleaner is used for $2$ hours and $36$ minutes each week.
